systems.name: Voice-Leading Harmony System
systems.summary: Roberts's central system treats chord melody not as vertical chord placement but as the simultaneous management of four independent melodic lines. The taxonomy of members spans voicing density (close vs. open), motion types (parallel, contrary, counter), and textural devices (block chords, sustained backgrounds, common tones, short punctuations). Rules govern how the guitarist moves between chords (preferring voice-leading continuity, delaying finger release, sustaining common tones) and how voicings are modified (converting close to open by octave displacement, dropping tones while relying on listener harmonic memory, substituting diminished for dominant 7b9). The system's governing logic is horizontal rather than vertical: chords are the momentary convergence of lines always in motion, and every rule ultimately serves melodic continuity.

members.name: Close Block Voicing
members.summary: Notes packed tightly together; used as textural contrast against open voicings.

members.name: Open Voicing
members.summary: Notes spread apart by octave displacement of one or more tones.

members.name: Parallel Motion
members.summary: All chordal tones moving the same number of scale steps in the same direction.

members.name: Contrary Motion
members.summary: Chordal tones moving in opposite directions simultaneously.

members.name: Counter Line
members.summary: Melodic accompaniment line, typically in the second voice from the top, most active when the main melody is static.

members.name: Block Chords
members.summary: A full chord placed under each melody note, with voicing or inversion changed with each new note.

members.name: Sustained Chord Background
members.summary: One chord held through two or more melody notes, with tones dropped only as fingering demands.

members.name: Common Tone
members.summary: A single note sustained across a sequence of successive chords.

members.name: Short Chord Punctuation
members.summary: Brief harmonic accents placed with authority within the bar to imply harmonic flow without constant restriking.

members.name: Two-Note Dyad
members.summary: Two-note voicing implying harmony, particularly in improvisation contexts.

traversal_rules.name: Four-Voice Melodic Motion
traversal_rules.summary: Move between chords by treating all four chordal tones as independent melody lines, connecting them through parallel, contrary, or counter motion.

references.topic: Voice leading is primary connective force
references.quote_excerpt: one is really dealing with four separate melody lines

traversal_rules.name: Sustain and Delay Finger Movement
traversal_rules.summary: Keep fingers in place until absolutely necessary to move, maximizing chord-tone sustain to generate melodic and harmonic continuity.

references.quote_excerpt: keep your fingers in place until it's absolutely necessary to move them

traversal_rules.name: Counter Line Activation on Static Melody
traversal_rules.summary: When the main melody has little motion, activate the counter line (second voice from top) to maintain horizontal interest.

references.quote_excerpt: When the main melody has little motion, the counter line can be more active

traversal_rules.name: Block Chord Voicing Change Per Melody Note
traversal_rules.summary: Change voicing or inversion with each new melody note so all lines appear to move together, achieving the block chord effect.

references.topic: Block chord effect: voicing must move with melody
references.quote_excerpt: change the voicing or inversion with each new melody note, in order to create the effect of all lines moving at once

traversal_rules.name: Counter Line Developmental Evolution
traversal_rules.summary: Inner voices evolve progressively from passing tones to counter lines to fully melodic patterns across a phrase.

references.topic: Counter line development into melodic pattern
references.quote_excerpt: extension of the passing tones into a more melodic pattern

traversal_rules.name: Octave Jump for Register Navigation
traversal_rules.summary: Transpose the melody up an octave when the melody sits too low to accommodate chord voicing below it, executed with finesse to preserve melodic continuity.

references.quote_excerpt: transpose the melody up an octave (this is called "jumping octaves") several times throughout the course of a solo

modification_rules.name: Close-to-Open Voicing Conversion by Octave Displacement
modification_rules.summary: Convert a close voicing to an open voicing by moving one or more chordal tones up or down an octave as far as reach permits.

references.quote_excerpt: moving one or more chordal tones up or down an octave

modification_rules.name: Drop Chord Tones Relying on Listener Harmonic Memory
modification_rules.summary: When sustaining a chord through a long melody sequence, drop chord tones as fingering demands, trusting listener memory to complete the harmonic outline.

references.quote_excerpt: the listener usually remember those notes that have been dropped

modification_rules.name: Diminished Chord Substitution for Dominant 7b9
modification_rules.summary: Replace a dominant 7b9 chord with a diminished chord to inject chromaticism into otherwise diatonic lines.

references.topic: Diminished chords as chromatic substitution for dominant
references.quote_excerpt: Eo and Dbo chords are both functioning as A7b9, and are being used to provide some chromatic relief

modification_rules.name: Extensions as Color Without Functional Change
modification_rules.summary: Add major 7th, 6th, 9th, and other extensions freely to enrich voicing color and texture without altering the chord's scale function or role in the progression.

references.topic: Role of chord extensions in diatonic function
references.quote_excerpt: addition of the extensions Maj. 7th, 6th, 9th, etc., only affect the color and texture of the chord

modification_rules.name: Chromatic Passing Chord Harmonization
modification_rules.summary: Connect diatonic progression points with chromatic passing chords (including altered forms like m7+5) as connective tissue, even when momentarily dissonant.

references.quote_excerpt: connected by the passing chords G#m7+5, Am7+5
Any chromatic note within finger range can always be harmonized with a given chord form, although it may occasionally be dissonant

modification_rules.name: Close Voicing as Textural Contrast
modification_rules.summary: Deploy close voicings deliberately as textural contrast against the broader sound of open voicings.

references.quote_excerpt: These can be used as texture contrast to the big sound of open voicings

modification_rules.name: Short Punctuation for Harmonic Continuity
modification_rules.summary: Use brief chord accents placed with authority within the bar to imply harmonic flow, reinforced by emphasizing chord tones in the melody.

references.topic: Short chord punctuations and harmonic continuity
references.quote_excerpt: outline the flow of harmony by short chord punctuations... played with authority and appropriately placed within the bar

modification_rules.name: Fourth String Register Floor
modification_rules.summary: The fourth string is the absolute lower limit for low-register melody playing with any chord fragment beneath it.

references.quote_excerpt: play a low register scale or melody (as low as the 4th string but no lower) with some fragment of the chord beneath

systems.name: Fingering Selection System
systems.summary: Roberts's secondary system governs how the guitarist chooses between alternative fingerings for any given passage. The taxonomy spans two competing criteria — musical quality (tone and sustain) and mechanical efficiency (avoidance of unnecessary movement) — held in deliberate tension. The traversal rule for string selection prefers greater vibrating string length for sustain and singing tone. The modification rule counters over-reliance on efficiency by prescribing that radical position jumps and large intervals are legitimate and expressive techniques, not failures of economy. The paired-principle structure — stating a criterion, then immediately qualifying it with its counterweight — is the system's defining logic.

members.name: Musical Quality Criterion
members.summary: Evaluate fingerings by tone, sustain, and expressive result.

members.name: Mechanical Efficiency Criterion
members.summary: Evaluate fingerings by elimination of unnecessary or awkward hand and finger movements.

members.name: Position Jump / Large Interval Leap
members.summary: Radical shift between fingerboard positions; a legitimate expressive technique providing contrast to smooth scalar movement.

traversal_rules.name: Prefer Greater Vibrating String Length
traversal_rules.summary: Choose the string set that maintains the greater vibrating string length, allowing notes to sing and sustain longer.

references.topic: Rule: choosing strings for sustain and tone
references.quote_excerpt: choosing a fingering or a set of strings in which the greater string length is maintained

modification_rules.name: Permit Radical Jumps for Expressive Contrast
modification_rules.summary: Do not suppress large position jumps or interval leaps in pursuit of efficiency; they are frequently required techniques and supply expressive contrast to smooth scalar movement.

references.topic: Principle: do not fear radical jumps or large intervals
references.quote_excerpt: do not also develop a fear of radical jumps or large intervals on the fingerboard
